Here are some of the important healthcare stories from this week:
UnitedHealth raises 2026 earnings guidance as lower costs drive Q3 earnings beat
UnitedHealth Group (UNH) reported better-than-expected third-quarter results and

for the third time this year.The largest U.S. health insurer lifted its full-year 2026 adjusted earnings outlook to at least $20.50 per share, which is above the consensus estimate of $19.87 and up from a previous range of $19.50 to $20.For the third quarter, the Eden Prairie, Minnesota-based managed care giant reported adjusted earnings of $4.69 per share, beating analyst estimates by $0.55. Revenue came in at $112.7B, down 0.4% year over year but ahead of consensus expectations by $1.21B.By segment, UnitedHealthcare, the company’s insurance unit, reported third-quarter revenue of $86.3B, down from $87.1B in the year-earlier period. Optum Health revenue fell 10% Y/Y to $22.9B, reflecting a reduction in value-based care patients served in markets where the business lacked sufficient value-based care presence to sustain its clinicians.
J&J raises full-year earnings guidance
Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) reported third-quarter results broadly in line with expectations and

and adjusted earnings guidance.The company now expects adjusted earnings for the full year to be in the range of $11.05 to $11.15 a share ($11.10 at midpoint), up from a prior expectation of $10.96 to $11.11. Sales are estimated in the range of $101.0B – $101.4B, implying a midpoint of $101.2B and up from a prior view of $100.8B – $101.4B.For the third quarter, Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) reported revenue of $25.4B, up 5.9% year over year, while adjusted earnings of $2.59 per share beat analyst estimates by $0.06. Revenue was in line with consensus expectations.
Roche signs $1.16B obesity drug deal with China’s Rona Therapeutics
Swiss drugmaker Roche (RHHBY)

params.linkText: signed an exclusive worldwide licensing agreement

children: with Chinese biotechnology company Rona Therapeutics for an experimental obesity drug candidate, in a deal worth up to $1.16B.Under the agreement, Rona will receive an upfront payment of $100M and is eligible for up to $1.06B in development, regulatory, and commercial milestone payments, along with tiered royalties on global net sales.The RNAi therapy targets ALK7, a protein involved in fat storage and metabolism. Rona said the treatment could reduce visceral and ectopic fat while preserving lean mass, potentially complementing existing incretin-based obesity drugs.The deal strengthens Roche’s obesity drug pipeline as it competes with Eli Lilly (LLY) and Novo Nordisk (NVO).
STERIS to buy Xodus Medical for $2.1B

STERIS (STE) said its wholly owned subsidiary has agreed to acquire Pennsylvania-based surgical products company Xodus Medical for $2.1B at closing, with the deal expected to be financed primarily through debt and close by Dec. 31, 2026, subject to customary conditions and regulatory approvals.The transaction is expected to generate tax benefits with a net present value of about $300M, bringing the net purchase price to approximately $1.8B. Xodus Medical could also receive up to $150M in additional earnout payments tied to performance targets in 2028.Xodus Medical is expected to generate approximately $245M in revenue and $135M in adjusted EBIT in calendar year 2026. STERIS said it will update its fiscal 2027 outlook to include the acquisition after closing.
Nvidia-backed drug discovery firm Iambic climbs on trading debut
Iambic Therapeutics
, a life sciences company backed by Nvidia
and AbbVie
, among others, rose more than 10% above its initial public offering price on Thursday in its first trading session as a listed firm.
Iambic
) shares opened at $16.15 at about 12 pm ET, roughly unchanged from the IPO price, then quickly added about 11% to reach $17.95 about an hour later, implying a valuation of roughly $876M.

Late Wednesday, the San Diego-based AI-driven drug discovery firm priced the offering of roughly 9.4M shares at $16.00, targeting about $150M in gross proceeds. A 30-day option was available for underwriters to purchase up to ~1.4M shares additionally at the IPO price adjusted for underwriting discounts and commissions.
Iambic

expects the offering to generate about $135M in net proceeds, which it intends to use, among other things, to advance its lead asset IAM1363. The oral tyrosine kinase inhibitor is currently undergoing a Phase 1/1b clinical trial for advanced HER2-altered solid tumors ahead of a potentially registrational study expected to begin next year.
CVS to pay $315M to feds over opioid prescription allegations
CVS Health

has reached an agreement with the Justice Department to resolve allegations that it illegally filled prescriptions for opioids and then sought payment for them from Medicare and other federal programs.

The settlement resolves a case filed by the federal government in 2024 that accused the pharmacy chain since at least October 2013 of "routinely [dispensing] controlled substances pursuant to prescriptions that were not valid, were not for a medically accepted indication, were not medically necessary, and/or were not issued in the usual course of professional practice.

"These included illegitimate prescriptions for extremely high doses and excessive quantities of potent opioids that fed dependence and addiction, as well as illegitimate prescriptions for dangerous combinations of opioids and other drugs."
The suit stated that from 2015 to 2020, CVS sold more than 12 billion doses of opioids.
